**READ-ONLY. Modify no files. No commits, no staging, no npm install, no npm start (a dev server is already running on :3000 and belongs to the developer). Do not run `npm run lint` with appended args.**

## Your spec
`.claude/skills/code-quality/SKILL.md` → "Agent B — Import analysis". Read it. Your rubric is the repo's own rules:
- `.claude/rules/conventions.md` → **Imports** section (no circular imports; no `../../../..` chains longer than 3 levels; no imports from internal `node_modules/@salesforce/...` source paths — use published entrypoints; no imports from a later-sprint feature)
- `.claude/rules/overrideStyling.md` → **"Importing an already-overridden component from a new component"** section. This is the highest-value check you have. It says an override that imports an *already-overridden* component must use a **relative path**, not the `@salesforce/retail-react-app/app/components/<name>` base path, because the `ccExtensibility` resolver only runs in the real app build — Storybook (`.storybook/main.js` aliases the package straight to `node_modules`) and Vitest (`vitest.config.ts` doesn't touch it) will silently render/test the **unstyled base SFCC version**. A story or test that looks like it exercises the override actually doesn't. Note the doc records one **known, not-yet-fixed** instance: `product-tile/index.tsx`'s `DisplayPrice` import — that one is pre-existing and out of this branch's scope; report it only as context, not as a finding against this PR.
- `.docs/memory/sprintScope.md` for the later-sprint check (note: `.docs/memory/` may be stale — cross-check against reality before asserting a sprint violation).
- `.claude/rules/frozenFiles.md` and `.claude/rules/protectedFiles.md` for tier context on what's imported/modified.

## Additional checks specific to this branch
1. **The resolver trap, applied concretely.** For every import in scope that targets `@salesforce/retail-react-app/app/components/<name>` or `.../app/pages/<name>`, check whether an override exists at the mirrored path under `overrides/app/`. If it does, that's a finding — and escalate it to 🔴 if a story or test in the repo actually renders the importing component (i.e. the wrong component is really being exercised). Enumerate what exists under `overrides/app/components/` before concluding.
2. **`overrides/app/routes.tsx` is Tier 2** (protectedFiles.md → Global Shell). Check what its diff does — is the product-detail route wired correctly, and is the import style consistent with the rest of the file (base path vs relative)?
3. **`overrides/app/utils/richText.tsx`** — conventions.md → Utilities says "No imports from `overrides/app/hooks/`". Also check the `dangerouslySetInnerHTML` sanitizer rule in conventions.md → General if this file renders HTML, and whether any new dependency was introduced (check `git diff origin/develop...HEAD -- package.json package-lock.json` — Hard Rule 7 forbids adding packages without approval).
4. **`overrides/app/types/vendor.d.ts`** — check what module declarations were added and whether they paper over a missing real type (which would be a `.claude/rules/typescript.md` concern worth reporting to me even though Agent C owns TS).
5. Check the import direction between the new `ui-kits` atoms/molecules, `product-view`, `product-detail/index.tsx`, `staticProductHeader.tsx`, `productInfo.ts` and `richText.tsx` for any cycle (one level deep is sufficient per the SKILL, but two levels is cheap here — do it).

## Settled decisions — do NOT report these as defects
- `product-view/index.tsx` and `pages/product-detail/index.tsx` are copy-first TypeScript ports of base SFCC files; their base-inherited imports of modules that have **no** local override are correct and expected. Only flag a base-path import where an override actually exists.
- `product-view/index.tsx`'s default export is intentionally a faithful SFCC bridge; its added optional `renderHeader` slot is deliberate.
- `formatPrice` duplication between the page and `staticProductHeader.tsx` is known and settled.

## Output
Return findings directly as your final message (do NOT write any .md report file). For each: absolute `file:line`, the rule breached **with the relevant sentence quoted** from the rule file, and a concrete fix. Group 🔴 / 🟡 / 🟢. State what passed and what you could not check.

---
name: code-quality
description: Audit recently changed or specified files for code quality issues — naming, circular imports, TypeScript coverage, test/story existence, and structural debt. Read-only. Use after implementing a feature or before opening a PR.
---

Audit code quality for the specified scope. Do not modify any files — this is a read-only
diagnostic. Produce a prioritised report with actionable fixes.

---

## Input

The user will provide one of:
- A file path or directory to audit
- No argument — default to files changed on the current branch: `git diff --name-only main`

If no argument is given, run: `git diff --name-only main` and audit those files.
Exclude test files (`*.test.ts`, `*.spec.ts`), stories (`*.stories.tsx`), and any registry files.

---

## Parallel execution

For audits covering more than 5 files, split into four independent checks and run them
as parallel agents simultaneously. Each agent receives only its own checklist — do not
bundle all checks into one agent.

- **Agent A — Naming & structure**
- **Agent B — Import analysis**
- **Agent C — TypeScript coverage**
- **Agent D — Test & story coverage**

For 5 files or fewer, run all checks sequentially in a single pass.

---

## Agent A — Naming & structure

Rules are defined once, split across [.claude/rules/conventions.md](../../rules/conventions.md)
(cross-cutting), [css.md](../../rules/css.md) (Chakra/styling), and
[components.md](../../rules/components.md) (components/hooks/Storybook) — read the relevant
ones first, then apply each rule to the files in scope. Do not re-list the rules here;
that's how the files drift apart.

Walk the file list and audit each file against the relevant section:

- Every file → conventions.md **General** section.
- Every file with JSX/Chakra props → css.md **Tokens** section (no hardcoded hex/px values).
- `.tsx` under `overrides/app/components/` or `overrides/app/pages/` → components.md
  **Components** + **Composition** sections, plus conventions.md **File naming and folder
  structure**.
- `.ts` under `overrides/app/hooks/` → components.md **Hooks** section.
- `.ts` under `overrides/app/utils/` → conventions.md **Utilities** section.

For each violation, record `file:line` and which rule file + bullet failed — the section
anchor is enough (e.g. "components.md → Components → Props type placement").

---

## Agent B — Import analysis

For each file, read the import statements and check:

- No circular imports: if File A imports from File B, File B must not import from File A
  (check by reading the imported file's imports in turn — one level deep is sufficient).
- No imports from a higher tier without justification:
  - A component must not import directly from internal `commerce-sdk-react` source paths.
  - A page must not bypass its own hooks to call raw API functions.
- No imports from a later-sprint feature (reference `.docs/memory/sprintScope.md` when present).
- No `../../../..` chains longer than 3 levels — flag for path alias review.

---

## Agent C — TypeScript coverage

Check each file against the relevant rule file:

- Every `.ts`/`.tsx` → [typescript.md](../../rules/typescript.md) in full (no `any` without
  justification, `type` vs `interface`, non-null assertions, discriminated unions, utility
  types, `import type`, `satisfies`, `readonly`, generic naming).
- Components → [components.md](../../rules/components.md) **Components** (props type name,
  placement, optional `?`, callback naming, JSDoc).
- Hooks → [components.md](../../rules/components.md) **Hooks** (typed params, explicit
  return type, JSDoc with `@returns`).

Then run `npx tsc --noEmit` **once** for the whole branch (not per file) and report any
errors. Cross-reference any new errors against the files in scope.

---

## Agent D — Test & story coverage

For each component file under `overrides/app/components/` or `overrides/app/pages/`:
- A paired `*.stories.tsx` exists in the same directory (required by [AGENTS.md](../../../AGENTS.md) > Testing).
- For logic-heavy components or hooks: the component's **own** `*.test.ts`/`*.test.tsx` exists
  in the same folder. A `play` function elsewhere (this component's own story, or — this is
  the common miss — a *different* component's assembly-level story) does not substitute for
  it, even when it happens to exercise the same rendered output; see testing.md's note under
  "What to test (and what to skip)". A component's own test file may still mock a hook or
  child component whose internals are covered elsewhere — the point is that the component's
  own render-branch/event-wiring contract has a test discoverable from its own folder.
- If a test file exists, verify:
  - At least one test covers the primary render case.
  - At least one test covers a user interaction (click, input) if the component has interactive elements.
  - No tests use `toBeTruthy()` as the sole assertion — check for meaningful assertions.
- If a paired `.stories.tsx` is missing, flag as MISSING STORY (mandatory).
- If a logic-heavy file has no test file of its own, flag as MISSING TEST — regardless of
  whether a `play` function exists somewhere else in the codebase.

For each utility file under `overrides/app/utils/`:
- **`.test.ts` required** when the utility has ≥1 conditional branch or performs ≥1
  transformation (currency, locale, mapping, parsing, etc.). Trivial re-exports and
  one-liners are exempt.
- If a test file exists, verify it covers both the happy path and at least one edge case
  (empty input, null, locale variation — whichever applies).

---

## Output format

Combine all agent results into a single prioritised report:

```
## Code Quality Report
**Scope:** [files audited]
**Branch:** [current branch]
**Date:** [today]

### 🔴 Must fix before PR merge
[Issues that would fail review or cause runtime errors — one line per issue with file:line]

### 🟡 Should fix in this PR
[Issues that affect maintainability or violate conventions — one line per issue with file:line]

### 🔵 Backlog (log, don't block)
[Minor style issues, missing test cases for edge cases — one line per issue]

### ✅ No issues found
[List checks that passed cleanly]

### Summary
X must-fix · Y should-fix · Z backlog items
```

Do not suggest refactors beyond the scope of the changed files.
Do not modify any files — report only.

## Doc-accuracy finding — worth escalating

**`overrideStyling.md`'s stated rationale for its most important rule is factually wrong**, and the two new files in this PR get it right.

`.claude/rules/overrideStyling.md:121-124` claims a base-path import "will build and run correctly in the shipped app, but silently render/test the unstyled base SFCC version in Storybook and Vitest." I verified against the resolver source, `node_modules/@salesforce/pwa-kit-dev/configs/webpack/overrides-plugin.js:128-146`:

```js
isFromExtends(request, filepath) {
  ...
  return this.extends.includes(pkgName) &&
    // request is not issued from overrides
    !filepath.includes(issuerPath)   // issuerPath = <projectDir>/overrides
}
```

When the issuer lives under `overrides/`, `isFromExtends` returns false, `targetFile` stays undefined, and the request falls through to base `node_modules` — **in every environment, including the real app build**. The plugin's own doc comment confirms this is deliberate ("allows the overrides to import from the base template using the same syntax"), and it must be, or `overrides/app/constants/index.ts`'s `export * from '@salesforce/retail-react-app/app/constants'` would resolve to itself.

Three consequences:
- The rule is **more** important than the doc implies — the failure is production, not just tooling.
- The doc's "dormant only because its Storybook story…" framing for `product-tile`'s `DisplayPrice` rests on the wrong reason; such an import would be live-broken in the app.
- That "known instance" also points at files that **don't exist here**: `overrides/app/components/product-tile/` and `.../link/` are absent on this branch and on `develop`. They exist only on unmerged branches (`04b65f6`, `0ca71d1`). Nothing for this PR to inherit or fix.

The comments at `product-detail/index.tsx:55-62` and `staticProductHeader.tsx:7-14` both state the correct mechanism and cite `isFromExtends` by name. The doc should be corrected to match the code, not the reverse.
